Shout-out to Stonemeier games for customer support.

I had, for years, been spending far too much on far too many games, a disease not entirely unheard of in our gaming circle. 

One game I picked up along the way was Viticulture essential, because medium weight 6 player games are at a premium for my group, and it looked like we might enjoy it. 

And we did...when we finally played it last month...a full decade after it was purchased.

Which is also when we happened to discover that the game was missing the green rooster, instead coming with two large green cellars.

So after game day I reached out to SMG and asked if there was any way at all to perhaps get said rooster. I mean, it's not like I was expecting anything from them, it has been over a decade for heaven's sake.

To my surprise and delight, less than two weeks later, a green rooster showed up in my mailbox.

This is remarkable from a customer service perspective. A decade!

In retaliation, I immediately purchased Tuscany and Moor and the extra workers and the metal coins for the game. That'll show em...how much I appreciate them.

Thank you, Dave at SMG. 

Y'all are a class act.

text:
Would you use a platform to contact board game publishers and pitch your games?

Hi everyone! I’m thinking about building a platform that brings together board game designers and publishers, and I’d like to understand whether it would solve a real problem.

The idea is to have a publisher database with contact details, the types of games they’re looking for, and submission guidelines. Designers could upload their sell sheets and submit them to publishers accepting pitches, keeping track of what they sent, to whom, when, and any responses they received.

I’d also like it to be useful at conventions, for submitting games and scheduling meetings without having to start over on a different platform for each event. The goal would be to keep everything in one place, rather than scattered across emails, attachments, and event-specific apps.

The ambition is for it to become a widely adopted resource within the industry. Obviously, the hardest part would be getting publishers on board.

For anyone who has pitched a game or works in publishing: would a platform like this make sense? How do you currently manage these contacts, and what difficulties do you run into? What would make you want to use it?

I intend to build it, but first I’d like to hear from potential users and understand what’s actually missing from the tools available today.
label: reasoned_advice

[iOS/Android] Castle Combo Digital version available

Hi r/boardgames!

I’m one of the developers at a small studio that adapts board games to mobile. The mods kindly gave me the OK to share this here (Thank you!). 

We previously released the digital version of Witchcraft!, and we’ve just launched our second adaptation: the official digital version of **Castle Combo**, the card drafting and tableau-building game by Catch Up Games (designed by Grégory Grard & Mathieu Roussel, illustrated by Stéphane Escapa).

This time, we didn’t want to just port it over as-is, so we put a lot of work into creating a **solo campaign** that offers a different way to enjoy the game, and we built different bot challenges so it still works great when you don’t have people around to play with.

My month of gaming. 14 out of 31 days played. Entropy was the biggest letdown and My Father’s Work was a surprise

Entropy felt like the mechanics didn’t fit the theme. They just felt generic. The game itself was ok, Worker placement with mitigations to resolve mini goals. There are a million little piles of tokens/components in this game too. 

My Father’s Work I owned for several years and never got around playing. I read that it was complicated and needed an app. Both scared me off back then. We decided to play this last week and overall we had a lot of fun. The App is mostly used to provide dialogue between the 3 rounds and also reveals a few decision results. Other games solve this with a book of secrets. The app could narrate more of the dialogue. And some of it could be a lot shorter but its easy enough to skip. The components are absolutely amazing. Glass vials, unique animal meeples, metal gears. And the dynamic story based worker placement spots are cool too. Whatever routine you used in round 1 might not be viable in round 2 because a spot went missing.
label: reasoned_advice

text:
The Thing vs Feed the Kracken

In less than 7 days, both of these titles will be hitting Gamefound. The closest thing to a hidden traitor/social deduction-esque game in my collection is Fury of Dracula (unless you count Nemesis). Almost 10 years ago I came very close to buying Infection at Outpost 31. I’ve loved The Thing since I was a kid, so I thought a board game of it could be very fun. Unfortunately I wasn’t into modern board games at the time, much less having a larger game group to play it with, so I passed (and I was also not into board games when the newer The Thing board game came out). Today, I have a pretty consistent gaming friend group of 4 and I imagine we could expand it to some other friends a few times a year to make it 6-8, so buying one of these types of games no longer feels totally unreasonable, but The Thing has been out of print since my friends started playing board games. 

I’ve also had Feed the Kraken on my potential list as it looks like a fun take on social deduction that doesn’t rely on IP as much (because ultimately you want everyone to have fun in these games, not just the fans of the IP). That said, the IP of The Thing is super appealing. I know Pendragon is woefully behind on some campaigns, but I’m hoping The Thing being a reprint helps de-risk the project some (though I do wonder why it even needs a crowdfunding at all vs print it and ship it to retail). Ultimately though, I want to get a game that will get tabled (as much as a larger player count game like this can reasonably be tabled) and for everyone to have a great time. 

Question is, for those of you that have / have played both, which do you prefer and why? If you were picking up only one, which one?
